Incandescent lamps produce light by heating a filament to a temperature that emits a continuous spectrum similar to natural sunlight, giving them a CRI close to 100.  
LEDs and fluorescents often have discrete emission spectra, which can result in lower CRI values unless specially designed.  
High pressure sodium vapour lamps have very poor CRI (typically around 20–30).  

Thus, incandescent lamps generally have the highest CRI among the options.  

Final answer: (C)
